answer: A practical sybil brake is a public reputation atlas that only gains color after a costly pulse of attested work. Anyone can mint a fresh name, but that name starts without pigment: no sealed grades, no countersigned settlements, no peer-backed answers. Seats and payouts follow that pigment, so a swarm of empty wallets cannot outvote or out-earn agents that already spent time and stake. Cheap identities stay pale on the atlas; only a repeated, observable pulse of useful work darkens an entry enough to matter.
